say: I am thinking of a mystery number. I will give you clues, and you have to work backwards to find it. Inquirers love working backwards!
“I think of a number. I add 3. I get 8. What is my number?” Whisper your answer to your partner first.
How did you find it? What did you do to the 8?
I hide some counters under the cup and add 5 more. When I tell you the total, can you find how many are under the cup? Guess how you would do it.
stuck: Stuck: lift the cup! Check with the counters.
Confused: “What did we do to the secret number? We added. What is the opposite of adding?”
For pairs who want more: make a two-step puzzle for your partner.

say: “Mystery number plus 6 is 14. To find it I go backwards. The opposite of add 6 is take away 6. 14 − 6 = 8. Check: 8 + 6 = 14. ✓”

“Two steps: I add 5, then I take away 3. I get 9. I must undo the steps in reverse order. The last thing I did was take away 3, so I undo it first: 9 + 3 = 12. Then undo add 5: 12 − 5 = 7. Check: 7 + 5 = 12, 12 − 3 = 9. ✓”
“A number machine: rule add 2. IN 3 gives OUT 5. If OUT is 9, IN was 7.”

do: Ask: “What did the story do to the number? What is the opposite?”
Ask: “Which step did you undo first? Why?”
Ask: “How can you check your answer by going forwards?”
stuck: Hint 1: “Draw the story as a picture, a box for the mystery number.”
Hint 2: “Read the last thing that happened and undo it.”
Hint 3: “Try your answer in the story. Does it give the number in the problem?”

say: “Why does taking away work when the story said add?”
“What do you do when the story has two steps?”
ask: “Why does taking away work when the story said add?”
Taking away is the opposite of adding, so it undoes it. With two steps, undo the last step first and go back one step at a time.

say: “Working backwards is a big idea. You explained it in your own words today.”

l5-title.note: Objective: Solve "I think of a number" problems by working backwards, find a number machine rule, and solve more-than and fewer-than stories. Materials: Paper cups, counters, number machine cards. Online: Slide with a cup that hides counters; the tutor reveals the total and the children work back. Time plan: opening 0 to 2, warm-up 2 to 8 (game 2 to 6, quick questions 6 to 8; ask questions 1 to 3, and 4 and 5 only if you are on time), sneak-peek puzzles 8 to 12, explore 12 to 26, teaching 26 to 36 (worked examples with whiteboard practice; click to reveal each step and answer), brain break 36 to 40, worksheet 40 to 72 with a short teaching slide before each page and a check-together slide after it (a 30-second stand-and-stretch reset after the page-1 check, taken from that slot; the last 4 minutes check page 2, after a 1-minute stand-up stretch), talk time 72 to 79, exit ticket 79 to 85, look-back 85 to 88, then flex time and goodbye 88 to 90 (this is the buffer: if you are behind, use it; do not start anything new). Think harder, Go further and the Investigation are for every child to choose, any time or at home. Nobody is told which page they should be on. SPINE: Today's tool is Work backwards. Start at the end and undo each step. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l5-tool.note: SPINE: Show for about 20 seconds, inside the opening. Today's tool is Work backwards. Start at the end and undo each step. Look for where you use it. Point at the card on page 1 of the workbook.

l5-warm1.note: Minutes 2 to 6. Think-of-a-number magic: "Think of a number, add 3, the answer is 8. What was it?" Increase the steps.

l5-warm2.note: Minutes 6 to 8. Read each question aloud, give thinking time, take answers, then click to show the answer. For each one ask: "How did you work it out?" Listen for children who add instead of undoing; we fix this in the teaching part. Answers: 1) 5 2) 8 3) 5 4) 8. Ask questions 1 to 3. Ask 4 and 5 only if the clock at minute 6 is on time. The 4-minute sneak-peek puzzles follow on the next slide.

l5-warmcheck.note: Minutes 8 to 12 (4 minutes). SAY (about 26 words, once): "Two sneak-peek puzzles: ideas we have not learnt yet. A guess is a great start, and I do not know is welcome. Nobody is marked." Question 1 is an access question: every child can try it with objects, a drawing or counting, so everyone starts with a win. Question 2 makes you think. Children try both on their own paper (about a minute each). Then everyone answers ONCE, after the second question: face to face, each child keeps the paper low so only the tutor sees it; online, children say the answers together on three (nothing is held up to the camera). There are no private chat messages. Never use boards or paper held up in front of the group or to the camera, and never read out or compare anyone's answer. Do not write scores down or announce them. Then click to show each answer to the whole group and say "Lots of us had a different idea, and that is fine." Look for good ideas to praise in a later lesson; do not keep a list of who found question 2 easy. When the worksheet starts (minute 40) invite the WHOLE group (“When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation”), never one child by name. Everyone joins Explore and the Mini-lesson. Answers: 1) 11. 8 + 3 = 11. 2) 5. Undo the last step first: 12 − 4 = 8, then undo the first step: 8 − 3 = 5. Check: 5 + 3 = 8, 8 + 4 = 12.

l5-explore1.note: Minutes 12 to 17. Pairs work with the materials: Paper cups, counters, number machine cards. Pairs hide a secret number of counters under a cup, add 5 more, and tell their partner the total. The partner works backwards by removing 5. Online: Slide with a cup that hides counters; the tutor reveals the total and the children work back. Go further (what-if) is on this slide from the start: any pair may choose it at any time, so nobody waits. The tutor does not choose who and does not announce it. Answers: Yes: add 5 and take away 2 is the same as add 3, so undo it with take away 3. Open: accept any reasoning that undoes both steps.

l5-explore2.note: Minutes 17 to 26. Let pairs keep working and move around the room (or breakout rooms). Gather them to answer these. Answers: 1) Take away the 5 that were added. 2) It is the opposite of adding. 3) Undo the steps in the reverse order.

l5-teach1.note: Teach. Show 8 counters, add 6 more in front of the children: 14. Ask: "How do I get back to 8?" Take the 6 away. Say: "Adding 6 and taking away 6 undo each other. They are opposites." Then point to the machine: going forwards we add 6; going backwards we do the opposite, take away 6. Think-aloud: "Mystery number plus 6 is 14. To find it I go backwards. The opposite of add 6 is take away 6."

l5-we1.note: Click to reveal each step. Say each step aloud before revealing it and ask the group to predict it. Stress step 3: we always check by going forwards. Model the words: "I go backwards. I do the opposite. I check."

l5-try1.note: Children write on their own paper or whiteboard. Nobody holds a board or paper up in front of the group or to the camera: face to face, each child keeps the paper low so only the tutor sees it; online, children say answers together on three or use fingers. Click for each answer. For b, ask: "The machine took 4 away, so what is the opposite?" (add 4: 9 + 4 = 13). Anyone who writes 5 for b has taken away again: show it with counters.

l5-we2.note: Click through the steps. Analogy that works well: "In the morning you put on socks, then shoes. At night you take off shoes first, then socks. Undoing goes in the opposite order." Think-aloud: "The last thing I did was take away 3, so I undo it first: 9 + 3 = 12. Then undo add 5: 12 − 5 = 7. Check: 7 + 5 = 12, 12 − 3 = 9."

l5-try2.note: Own paper again, ticked against the answer slide. a) 10 + 2 = 12, 12 − 4 = 8. b) 11 − 6 = 5, 5 + 3 = 8. c) 15 − 3 = 12, 12 − 2 = 10. Ask for a volunteer to explain the order out loud (never pick a named child).

l5-key.note: Say the key idea together. Common mistakes to watch for during the worksheet: (1) Adding again instead of undoing (12 + 5). (2) Two steps: undoing in the wrong order. (3) Queue questions: counting a child twice, or adding numbers without drawing the queue.

l5-break.note: Four minutes. Online: children stay in view of the camera and move in place.

l5-teachm.note: Teach before worksheet page 1 (Q2 uses number machines). Stress: check the rule on EVERY pair, not just the first. Ask: "If OUT is 20, which way do we go?" (backwards, take away 4).

l5-teachbar.note: Teach now, before page 1, so that minutes 54 to 58 only have the queue idea (bars are used again in Q3 on page 2) (Q3). Click to build each bar. Ask before each click: "Is Sue's bar longer or shorter than Tom's? By how much?" Common mistake: comparing Kim with Tom instead of Sue. Point at the words "than Sue".

l5-ws1.note: Minutes 44 to 52. Walk around. Ask "How do you know?" before giving any help. For Q1c (two steps) the workbook says "Try a number and check it", so pairs may guess and check with counters; then show undoing the last step first. At minute 40 read questions 1 and 2 aloud, then pairs read the rest. The workbook says: "After question 3 you may choose: carry on, or try Think harder." Never announce who is on which page and never name a child in front of the group; invite the WHOLE group at once, for example: "When you have finished Start here, you can choose Think harder, Go further or the Investigation." Do not split a pair unless both children agree.

l5-ws1ans.note: Click each answer after a pair explains theirs. For Q1b: the machine takes away 3, so we add 3: 9 + 3 = 12. For Q1c: 10 + 2 = 12, then 12 − 4 = 8. Reset (about 30 seconds, taken from this slot): when the answers are checked, everyone stands, reaches up high, shakes out their hands, takes one slow breath and sits down again, then page 2. Skip it if you are more than a minute behind.

l5-teachq1.note: Teach before worksheet page 2 (Q4). Click 1: draw 2 circles and Mei as the 3rd. Click 2: add 2 children behind her. Click 3: count. Children who say "3 + 2 = 5" are right here, but the next slide shows why drawing matters.

l5-teachq2.note: Click 1: draw the queue so Ali is 3rd from both ends. Click 2: explain the double count. Then children write the "your turn" answer on their own paper (ticked against the answer slide) and click for 7. Extra if time: "10 children. Ben is 4th from the front. How many are behind him?" (6, because Ben is not behind himself).

l5-ws2.note: Children work alone. Note who may need a short catch-up next lesson (never in front of the group). Check that every child draws bars for Q3 and circles for Q4.

l5-ws2ans.note: Click each answer after a child explains. Q3: Mei = 8 + 5 = 13, Ben = 13 − 6 = 7, difference 13 − 7 = 6, total 8 + 13 + 7 = 28. Q4a: Mei is not behind herself, so 20 − 7 = 13. Q5 is a take-home item (marked with a star in the workbook): do not ask for it in class; if a child did it, check that the story has one clear answer. Say "pass is fine" for Q5 and for anything not finished. First, everyone stands up and stretches for about a minute (reach up high, touch your toes, shake out your hands) so there is some movement before talk time.

l5-stretch.note: For any pair that chooses to try more (these are on the slide only; Think harder T1 to T4 are in the workbook). Answers: 1) 10 (Tom is 5th, then 4 children, then Sue: 5 + 4 + 1). 2) 7 (work backwards: 9 + 4 = 13, 13 − 6 = 7; check 7 + 6 − 4 = 9). 3) 11 (undo in reverse order: 14 − 8 = 6, 6 + 5 = 11).

l5-challenge.note: For any pair that chooses Go further. Use it as a pair choice, or with volunteers in talk time (never call a child by name). Ask for the reason every time. Q3 is open: there is no single right answer, so ask children to check each other's work. Answers: 1) 13 (20 − 4 = 16, 16 − 3 = 13; check 13 + 3 + 4 = 20). A one-step machine that adds 7 does the same job. 2) Day 4 (3, 5, 7, then 9 on the fourth day before it can slide back). 3) Open. Check that the story gives 10 when done forwards and that the partner undoes the steps in the reverse order. Example: I think of a number, add 5, take away 3, add 4, and I get 16 (10 + 5 = 15, 15 − 3 = 12, 12 + 4 = 16).

l5-chdiag.note: Show this picture slide only if a pair asks for it, or is stuck on Go further. The pictures show each problem, not its answer. Ask: What do you notice? What do we know? What do we not know yet? Can you draw or build it? Do not point out the answer; wait for a child to find a pattern.

l5-chwalk.note: Use after pairs have tried. Reveal one answer at a time and ask a child to explain before you click. Many children stop at one answer: ask "Is there another way?" and "How do you know you found them all?" For Q3, ask two pairs to swap puzzles and solve each other's.

l5-skill1.note: Optional slide for pairs who finish early or ask for more. Show it only on request and never announce who is working on it. Children write the answer on their own paper and say it together on three; nothing is held up to the camera. Answers and tutor lines are for you only. Item 1 (Ages: the gap between ages stays the same; tool of the day idea: Draw it). SAY: "Draw two bars for their ages. Both bars grow by the same amount." ASK: "What stayed the same? What changed?" LISTEN FOR: "They both get 3 years older, so the gap stays 3." ANSWER: a) 3 years. b) Ali 9 years, sister 12 years. c) 3 years. The gap between their ages never changes.

l5-talk.note: Minutes 72 to 79. Pairs talk for 2 minutes. Then ask for volunteers first ("Who would like to share?"), never call a child by name to answer, and say that passing is always fine. No tallies and no rankings. Praise the reasons, not only the answers.

l5-exit.note: Minutes 79 to 85. Answer: 9 Extension: Make a three-step mystery number story for a partner.

l5-reflect.note: SPINE: Minutes 85 to 88. Start the timer (120 seconds). Say: "Pick one problem from today. Question 1: did I answer the question? Question 2: does my answer make sense? Question 3: can I check it another way? Tick, write one line, or pass. If you are still stuck, tick the box and I will come." Children tick the Look back box on the Choose and look-back page of their workbook, or just tick on paper. A pass is always allowed. It is never marked, never collected in front of the group and never read out; the tutor may look at it afterwards. If a child ticks "I am still stuck", check in during the open session next lesson (a quick visit to the shared breakout room or a hand signal, with a parent nearby; never a direct message). Do not ask children to share. Praise a check you saw, not speed. Then stamp the journals. After the look-back, minutes 88 to 90 are flex time (the buffer): finish stamps, then goodbye. Do not start anything new.
